page.layout: One block of italic verse at the top, in two stanzas; below it an ornamental woodcut (not text); a single capital Greek mark in the right margin beside the lower part of the verse.

p.i: Nec sanctitati cedere gratiam, Nec sanctitatem cedere gratiæ.
Procede tandem:quid bona gaudia Vatum moraris? nec caput exere Tantùm: sed alto sidera, sidera, Mirande vates, incute vertice.

page.notes: The woodcut below the verse is a decorative ornament (a grotesque head with snakes and foliage, with hanging tassels), not text, so it is not transcribed. The right margin carries a capital Greek mark, read as ΕΙΣ; the spacing is uncertain. The faint mirrored text running down the right side of the page is show-through from the other side and is left out. No page number, running head, catchword or signature is visible.
